prs.title: fix: checkpoint adapter usage and preserve unknown prices
prs.author: devinfoley
prs.body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work.
> - Run accounting starts with receipts from each agent adapter.
> - A failed or interrupted process can lose usage. Missing provider prices can be mistaken for zero.
> - This pull request captures usage checkpoints and preserves unknown prices through adapter completion.
> - The server can recover usage without fabricating a free run or double-counting cumulative tokens.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Refs #14548, #12538, #212.

Stack order: #14989 → #14991 → #14994 → #14997 → #14999 → #15001. Part 2 of 6. Merged into `master` at `eab93fd4a077`.

## What Changed

- Add normalized usage checkpoints and explicit completeness to the adapter contract.
- Persist explicitly reported zero OpenCode usage before cleanup; missing or invalid counters remain incomplete and unpriced, including unterminated output.
- Preserve usage through failures, retries and multiple provider attempts across local adapters and ACPX.
- Count ordinary plus cached prompt input for the session-rotation threshold, preserving the exclusive split for billing; ten real heartbeat cases cover Codex/Gemini boundaries and historical inclusive rows. Persist an explicit raw-token layout marker so upgrades cannot count old cache hits twice.
- Separate ordinary and cached input tokens using each provider format. Preserve explicit zero prices and missing prices as distinct states, including later unpriced Gemini usage.
- Preserve the applied Codex fast pricing tier through checkpoints and terminal results, including safer retries.
- Classify managed custom Responses routes as API usage with their routed biller; retain unknown prices instead of treating them as ChatGPT subscriptions or direct OpenAI.
- Prevent sandbox transports from replaying an already-streamed capped output tail into accounting.
- Mark prompt/metadata failures before provider dispatch as no-work bootstrap failures, while uncertain dispatch failures stay incomplete.
- Persist Codex terminal checkpoints before forwarding logs; missing or invalid usage remains incomplete and unpriced, including failed turns. Explicit zero counters remain valid.
- Preserve incomplete Cursor usage and Codex native report completeness without inventing zero counters or borrowing missing counters from an earlier report.
- Preserve malformed optional counters through checkpoint projection using a content-free invalid marker; real Codex/Cursor/OpenCode execution regressions preserve incomplete accounting without storing malformed text.
- Add parser, callback and real child-process failure tests. Prevent sandbox test fixtures from silently installing a real CLI if discovery fails; isolate command-discovery tests from the separately tested callback bridge.

## Verification

- Run `pnpm test:run` for adapter parser, execution and failure-path suites.
- Inspect interruption tests for the difference between partial checkpoints and a complete receipt.

Integrated-stack validation on master `c365a16e346d`: repository-wide typechecking and production build, token gates, 313 focused accounting tests, two historical migration tests, four required SIGKILL cases and four mutation sentinels pass. The thirteen accounting modules meet their individual coverage floors (aggregate 99.7% lines, 94.82% branches). CI fixture regressions pass 48 connection-card cases, both recovery release orders and the personal-connection browser workflow. Final consumer regressions pass all 28 Browser Use lifecycle, 42 email pipeline and 140 rendered issue-detail cases; local email verification used this checkout’s bundled skills to avoid an unrelated ancestor skills directory. Merged-source regressions pass AI connections (107), route authorization (23), worktree cloning (63) and ACPX execution (221). Additional checks during stack preparation passed native execution (565), heartbeat admission (60), OpenCode/checkpoint/failure-path (102), Codex runner drivers (316) and Costs UI (21). Runtime/connection (644), adapter/billing (86), all Codex adapter cases (509 passed, one skipped), dashboard (106), worktree-cloning (63), CLI cost (14) and gate-harness (48) tests pass. Release workflow tests (18) and actionlint pass; frozen-install shell regressions confirm current locks proceed and stale locks fail without retries. The repository lockfile bot must land the coverage dependency refresh before frozen-install workflows run. All three accounting browser workflows pass on the current merged tree; the Storybook build and populated provider/biller smoke check passed earlier in stack preparation. Landing validation against the six intervening master changes passes all 282 targeted UI tests, 18 workflow tests and repository-wide typechecking; Storybook host validation adds 19 passing cases and 18 live HTTP checks, with UI typechecking and token gates passing. After master consolidated Cursor support, the one cancellation overlap preserves both current-budget fencing and the new manual cancellation identities. All 642 affected heartbeat/cancellation/native/Cursor tests, repository-wide typechecking and production build pass after reinstalling the updated ACPX patch. > - The Costs API reports subscription quota for connected provider accounts.

prs.title: fix: make accounting durable and synchronize cost reporting
prs.author: devinfoley
prs.body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work.
> - Costs and budgets must agree on one durable company ledger.
> - Interrupted runs, duplicate receipts, rounded amounts and concurrent budget updates can lose or misstate spend.
> - This pull request makes accounting durable and exact and updates the dashboard with its API contract.
> - Retries preserve one charge, unknown prices remain visible, and budget decisions use consistent totals.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Refs #14548, #5598, #12538, #212, #11419, #9433. Includes the performance work previously reviewed in #15125.

Stack order: #14989 → #14991 → #14994 → #14997 → #14999 → #15001. Part 4 of 6. Merged into `master` at `799e4d556f5c`.

## What Changed

- Capture fsynced usage receipts, verify directory ancestry before provider dispatch, replay after failures and acknowledge only after atomic ledger settlement. Preserve a complete streamed receipt when the bounded final output loses it, without hiding additional usage or charges.
- Use exact decimal cents, idempotency identities, immutable run attribution and explicit reported/estimated/unpriced states.
- Estimate supported Codex models with pricing provenance. Preserve pending or unpriced usage when a reliable total is unavailable.
- Make reservations, incidents, projections, cancellation delivery and hire-approval lock ordering consistent under concurrency.
- Add user attribution, read-only snapshot reporting, invoice reconciliation, provider report import and recovery/inspection APIs while preserving existing Finance ingestion and access rules.
- Include the performance fixes in the initial implementation: avoid reporting write locks, coalesce recovery and limit policy scans to the relevant scope.
- Add one generated, replay-safe migration and historical upgrade, pricing, budget and heartbeat tests. Additional fault/concurrency gates follow in #15001.
- Ship the final shared Costs page with its API: agent/user/project tables, estimate labels, safe stale refreshes and currency-aware Finance cards.
- Keep Recent financial events on Finance only, compact the agreed labels/layout and collapse advanced budget settings. No new accounting-health or charge-entry panels.
- Show exact estimated run charges in agent/issue views and safely format invalid historical currency codes.
- Require fresh complete native per-run usage for the terminal turn; stale attachment snapshots and partial reports remain pending. Save terminal receipts before committing the native result, including when replaying durable events.
- Accumulate native OpenCode turns across retries and controller restarts from durable run events, preserving cumulative Codex semantics, exact price sums, replay safety and incomplete evidence.
- Retain a successful Claude retry’s known model breakdown when the rejected resume reports complete zero spend and zero tokens.
- Recheck current budgets and manual pauses before native recovery reuses a reservation; compare exact cents for daily heartbeat cost caps.
- Settle Browser Use charges, Finance entries, projections and cumulative checkpoints under the company accounting lock; preserve rollback and idempotent retry on failure.
- Keep task and subtree token totals consistent with historical and current cache layouts, and compare exact decimal spend during email admission.
- Preserve historical Pi/OpenCode exclusive input counts while normalizing legacy Codex inclusive counts.
- Restore saved zero budgets when a positive limit is saved, preserve disabled positive policies when their amounts change, retain known partially unpriced user spend, and invalidate all company reporting periods on live cost events.
- Take the attributed issue lock before the run lock during native settlement and recheck attribution, with concurrent PostgreSQL regressions.
- Keep overlapping invoice evidence out of Finance totals; retain unique charge links and require review for ambiguous matches or changed prices.
- Serialize agent deletion before child locks and preserve existing charged-agent deletion restrictions.
- Serialize company deletion with accounting writers using a foreign-key-compatible lock; remove Finance/cost/budget dependencies before runs and approvals. Preserve native result writes and atomic rollback when existing native-artifact constraints prevent deletion.
- Persist a sticky incomplete-accounting marker when checkpoint capture or completion fails, await it before surfacing rejection, retry it before heartbeat failure finalization, and prevent replay, replacement or finalizer readiness from settling an older receipt. Fence stale recorders by company, run and source identity.
- Preserve empty-turn task recovery when an explicitly complete zero-usage receipt carries the completeness flag. Keep partial, malformed and nonzero usage conservative. Do not let a zero-cost empty attempt suppress the estimate for later paid Codex usage.
- Carry explicit runner usage completeness into native accounting. Accumulate ACPX per-turn reports across retries and controller recovery, preserving missing evidence and valid zero usage.
- Retain the upstream 0307 migration snapshot when adding accounting migration 0312.
- Keep interrupted AgentCore receipts pending while usage metadata is missing or token counts remain lower bounds; reject conservative ceiling/unknown/pending markers before certifying run deltas.
- Accept fractional cents in shared status-card daily/update and skill-test cost summary schemas while preserving nonnegative finite values and integer token counters.
- Emit managed Claude and AWS AgentCore per-run receipts from a durable session baseline. Preserve it across retries/recovery, rotate it only for a new run, reject incomplete or regressing totals, and retain AgentCore estimate labels.
- Restrict external provider billing imports to active company owners/admins or instance/local operators. Require a dedicated company secret explicitly designated for the matching billing provider and account before resolving its value.
- Generate accounting migration 0312 after the newly landed MCP migration; retain the proven replay-safe accounting SQL and verify schema drift.
- Load routine route test dependencies after mock registration to avoid a reproduced importActual race; keep the existing authorization and telemetry assertions.

## Verification

- `pnpm test:run` exercises the database, receipt, native execution, reporting, budget and migration suites.
- The integrated branch passed historical migration, user attribution, performance and AI connection tests. The routing and Costs page regressions are included with the production changes; latest Costs/live-update suites pass all 83 cases. The final coverage gate is in #15001.
- Full-stack browser tests passed for real run settlement, budget stop/resume and retained Finance API ingestion.
- A PostgreSQL regression reproduces a complete zero-cost resume followed by a paid retry whose spool write fails before complete(); the run stays pending and the reservation held. Additional tests cover validation/completion failure, replay, replacement, stale controllers and transient database fence failures, including actual heartbeat failure finalization.
- The empty-turn regression fails in both prepared modes through the real translator; the zero-then-paid pricing regression fails both with and without restart before the fixes. All 601 native executor tests and166 runtime/driver tests pass afterward, with repository-wide typecheck and build. Existing Linux Runner and browser CI passed the preceding completeness revision.
- ACPX regressions fail before the fixes: six incomplete-receipt cases, eight multi-turn/recovery cases, and seven runner translation/driver assertions. All 593 native executor tests pass after the fixes; complete Codex ACPX totals remain eligible for an exact token-price estimate. Repository-wide typecheck and production build pass.
- All 15 Rust

prs.title: fix: fence accepted work and cleanup before idle sleep
prs.author: devinfoley
prs.body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work.
> - A host can stop an idle instance to reduce unused compute.
> - Zero active runs do not prove that requests, saved work, or cleanup are complete.
> - A client can disconnect while its request still writes, and failed cleanup can remain only in memory or on disk.
> - This pull request holds new admission and checks accepted work, cleanup, and persisted work under an owned drain.
> - The host gets an empty report only while those checks remain valid.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Refs #13413. That companion PR uses the same owned-hold vocabulary for runtime services. This PR covers HTTP requests, scheduler work, accounting, cleanup, and the instance work inventory. It does not include the preview gateway changes.

**What existing behavior does this improve?**

The instance task-drain API reports process counters. It does not prove that a host can safely stop the instance for idle sleep.

**Current behavior**

A quiet run set can coexist with an unfinished request, cleanup after a completed run, future work, or a failed accounting write.

**Proposed behavior**

Provide a bounded owned idle hold. Block new ingress, track accepted handler promises, inspect durable and local work, and return `none` only when the same hold stays quiet through the checks. Keep normal deployment drains compatible.

**Reason and benefit**

Hosts can identify eligible idle instances without treating a disconnect or failed cleanup write as completed work.

## What Changed

> - Automatic idle sleep must preserve accepted work and unfinished cleanup.

prs.title: fix: checkpoint database backups before idle sleep
prs.author: devinfoley
prs.body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip coordinates agent work and preserves company state.
> - Hosted instances can stop compute when admission and all work sources are quiet.
> - The periodic database backup timer currently blocks every automatic sleep.
> - Disabling backups would remove recovery points.
> - This change offers an explicit final-backup checkpoint before sleep.
> - A verified archive and restart marker preserve recovery while compute is stopped.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

**What happened?**

An otherwise idle instance with automatic backups enabled always reports background work. Operators cannot reclaim idle compute without disabling those backups. The work inventory also queries the database before checking known local blockers.

**Expected behavior**

An operator can enable checkpoint mode. The server may authorize sleep only after all other work is quiet and a fresh backup is verified under the same owned hold. Backups resume on restart with the existing retention policy.

**Steps to reproduce**

Acquire a bounded idle drain on an instance with no application work and automatic backups enabled. Read its owned idle safety report. It reports present even when all other work is clear. With this change and `PAPERCLIP_DB_BACKUP_IDLE_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED=1`, a successful final backup can permit sleep; backup failures still refuse it.

**Paperclip version or commit**

Reproduced from master at 4265cb3a2b.

**Deployment mode**

Hosted single-process instances with persistent backup storage and serialized sleep/wake operations.

Searched open backup and sleep PRs and issues. Related: #15522 and #15599 establish owned idle holds and plugin drains. #15358 proposes general backup health/retention validation; this change verifies only opted-in sleep checkpoints and their restart catch-up.

## What Changed

- Add an off-by-default checkpoint flag. Keep automatic backups enabled.
- Reject known local blockers before database work.
- Finish a new backup during each owned safety check, including final revalidation.
- Verify the complete gzip archive and sync its file and directory before pruning older recovery points.
- Use unique checkpoint filenames so repeated checks cannot replace an earlier verified archive.
- Keep backup work counted through dump, validation and persistence. Changed owners, expired holds, concurrent work and errors refuse sleep.
- Persist a restart marker before the dump. Attempt a fresh backup on restart before idle eligibility, then resume the normal timer. Only a verified fresh backup clears the marker.
- Restrict managed checkpoint reads to verified Cloud control actors. Tenant instance-admin elevation does not grant backup authority.
- Keep archive verification outside engine fallback so failures retain their original cause.
- Document that recurring duplicate archives pause while asleep. The final checkpoint and historical archives remain on persistent storage; retention does not prune while asleep.

## Verification

- Focused idle, spool, backup and route checks: 137 tests passed, including restoration into a separate PostgreSQL database.
- Backup library and checkpoint tests: 15 passed, including rejection before historical backups can be pruned.
- `pnpm -r typecheck` and `pnpm build` passed. Follow-up server typecheck and database build cover the verification callback.

All five passed from an isolated checkout at 949210 (3 targeted chat/tool checks and the complete 39-test email suite). The redundant local run was stopped after final-head hosted CI passed. Live staging activation awaits merge and a canonical image; no production configuration or deployment changed.

prs.title: perf(server): stop polling five empty delivery queues
prs.author: cryppadotta
prs.body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip manages work for companies of AI agents.
> - Its server must deliver saved feedback, answers, and continuation receipts.
> - Five delivery queues scan the database on a fixed interval even when empty.
> - These queries keep idle databases active and add traffic to hosted instances.
> - This pull request wakes those queues from the transaction that creates work.
> - Startup recovery and retries still protect unfinished delivery.
> - Empty queues stop their timers and wait for the next committed write.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

**What existing behavior does this improve?**

Background delivery of feedback exports, chat completions, connection continuations, question answers, and tool-action receipts.

**Subsystem affected**

`server/` orchestration and `packages/db` transaction handling.

**Current behavior**

Feedback exports scan every five seconds. Four other queues scan on the heartbeat scheduler interval, normally 30 seconds. Empty queues still query the database.

**Proposed behavior**

Subscribe before startup recovery. Wake the queue when its producer transaction settles. Run only one sweep per queue at a time. Keep a recovery timer while work remains or a query fails. Stop the timer after a successful empty scan.

**Reason and benefit**

Remove avoidable idle SQL and network traffic without dropping durable delivery records. This is a first step toward instance sleep; other loops remain.

**Breaking changes**

No schema or HTTP contract changes. Notifications are local to one `createDb` instance and its transactions. Independent SQL clients and other server replicas cannot wake this consumer. Their writes require a separate notification/recovery design. Current server service writers are covered.

**Additional context**

Related: #15599 handles plugin drain before sleep. #15391 handles plugin readiness and lifecycle hints. Neither replaces these delivery queue scans.

## What Changed

- Add transaction-aware work signals to `createDb`, including nested transactions and caller-owned transactions. Publish before route or activity side effects can fail.
- Use one shared worker implementation for the five queues. Coalesce signals, prevent overlapping sweeps, track active work for idle admission, and await work on shutdown.
- Remove the five empty-queue polling paths. Retain existing durable claims, retry behavior, and startup reconciliation.
- Serialize route and worker feedback flushes to prevent duplicate concurrent uploads.
- Save the sleep inventory and record this first migration and its remaining work.

## Verification

- `pnpm -r typecheck` passed. Direct database and server typechecks passed after the final changes.
- `pnpm build` passed. The changed database and server packages were rebuilt successfully at the final commit.
- Six existing delivery integration suites: 259 tests passed against temporary PostgreSQL.
- Added assertions for all five producer signals. The completion journey proves dispatch without a route callback and recovery after consumer restart. A fixture initially left the first reporting turn unadmitted; after correcting that fixture, all 44 completion tests passed.
- Final commit-signal and worker tests: 15 passed. These cover nested and concurrent transactions, rollback, ambiguous commit, enqueue/empty-check races, retries, shutdown, drain/standby, and an hour of simulated empty-queue inactivity.
- Startup wiring regression suite passed. Worker and idle-sleep safety regressions: 51 tests passed.
- Full local `pnpm test:run` was stopped after all final-head hosted checks passed. It reported one 15-second conversation-route timeout; all 40 tests in that file passed on isolated rerun. No clean full local-suite pass is claimed.
- Greptile completed on `90619cdeaf2c021566cbef8f508ae5d87b033e38`: 5/5, no actionable findings, zero review threads. All 56 final-head check/status entries are clean (success or intentional skip), including the complete hosted test matrix, build, typecheck, end-to-end tests, canary, and security checks.

- The first hosted workspace attempt hit a temporary PostgreSQL connection refusal in a CLI worktree fixture. Its one rerun passed. All other hosted jobs passed on the first final-head attempt. A local reproduction stopped earlier at embedded PostgreSQL initialization and did not reproduce the same CI failure.

- This removes empty scans, not all polling. Outstanding or blocked deliveries, including pending tool reviews, retain recovery checks. Review expiry and execution scans are unchanged.
- A lost commit acknowledgement leaves a conservative recovery timer and idle-admission hold active until restart. A consumer started later inherits that uncertainty. An empty read cannot prove that the uncertain commit will not become visible later.
- New producers must signal through the same instrumented database scope. A persistent database listener is not introduced.
- This does not add the instance-wide scheduler or external waker and does not establish provider sleep or cost savings.

issues.title: Cost read endpoints never expose cost_status: a proven $0 cost is indistinguishable from an unknown cost
issues.author: panoskoun
issues.body:
## Summary

`cost_events.cost_status` is written, stored, and correct — and is then read by **nothing**. The column is never selected in a single cost read query, so every cost API returns `costCents: 0` with no way for a consumer to distinguish **"the cost is zero"** from **"we do not know the cost"**.

This makes `costs/summary` structurally incapable of supporting budget enforcement, and it is the same missing primitive that #5598 asks for under the name "NULL-usage guardrail".

## Environment

- `paperclipai` / `@paperclipai/server` **2026.916.1**
- Self-hosted, embedded Postgres
- Company: 4 agents, 1 project, 1 provider, 1 model, 9 `cost_events` rows, all `cost_status = 'reported'`

## The data is already there

`server/dist/services/costs.d.ts` — `createEvent` returns the field:

```ts
createEvent: (companyId, data) => Promise<{
    ...
    costCents: number;
    costStatus: string;   // <-- present on the write path
    ...
}>
```

`server/dist/services/heartbeat.js:3278` computes it:

```js
export function resolveLedgerCostStatus(input) {
    const hasTokenUsage = input.inputTokens > 0 ||
        input.cachedInputTokens > 0 ||
        input.outputTokens > 0;
    return input.costUsd == null && hasTokenUsage ? "unpriced" : "reported";
}
```

The logic is right: token usage present but no price ⇒ `unpriced`; an explicit `0` price ⇒ `reported`. A free model that genuinely reports `costUsd: 0` is correctly `reported`, and that is exactly the distinction that is currently thrown away at read time.

## The read path drops it

`server/dist/services/costs.js` — the string `cost_status` occurs **0 times**; `costStatus` occurs **0 times**. It is never projected in any query. Confirmed against the declared return types in `costs.d.ts`:

| method | returns `costStatus`? |
|---|---|
| `createEvent` | **yes** (write path only) |
| `summary` | no |
| `byAgent` | no |
| `byAgentModel` | no |
| `byProvider` | no |
| `byBiller` | no |
| `byProject` | no |
| `windowSpend` | no |
| `issueTreeSummary` | no |

Verified live against every cost read endpoint on a 2026.916.1 instance. Actual responses:

```
GET /costs/by-agent-model
[{ "agentId":"...","agentName":"Recruiter","provider":"opencode",
   "biller":"openrouter","billingType":"unknown",
   "model":"opencode/space-bunny-free","costCents":0,
   "inputTokens":240805,"cachedInputTokens":22905889,"outputTokens":166629 }]

GET /costs/summary
{ "companyId":"...","spendCents":0,"budgetCents":0,"utilizationPercent":0 }
```

`by-agent-model` is the worst case: it reports `costCents: 0` next to 25M tokens of usage. A consumer has no way to know whether that is a free model, a mispriced model, or a model whose price the registry has never heard of. All three look identical.

`summary` is worse: it returns no event count at all, so not only can you not count `unpriced` events, you cannot even compute an event-weighted rate limit.

## Why this blocks budget enforcement

`computeObservedAmount` reads `sum(cost_cents)`. On an all-free instance that is `0` forever, so the soft threshold, the hard stop, and `getInvocationBlock` are all unreachable — a budget policy set today would look armed and would never fire. That is the correct behaviour *for this instance*; it is the **reporting** that is broken. An operator cannot tell "my budget is not being consumed because the model is free" from "my budget is not being consumed because the meter is blind".

## Proposal

1. Add `costStatus` to the read projections in `costs.js` — at minimum `byAgentModel`, `byProvider`, `byAgent`, `byBiller`.
2. Add a derived `unpricedEventCount` to `summary` (and to the per-row endpoints as `unpricedEventCount`).
3. Add `eventCount` to `summary` so a `0` spend rate is interpretable without a second round trip.
4. Surface `unpriced` in the UI next to the cost figure rather than rendering a bare `0`.

Additive only — no existing field changes shape.

## Acceptance criteria (machine-checkable)

- [ ] `GET /costs/by-agent-model` returns a `costStatus` field per row, and it is populated for every row.
- [ ] `GET /costs/summary` returns `unpricedEventCount` and `eventCount`.
- [ ] Given a `cost_events` fixture with (a) `cost_cents = 0, cost_status = 'reported', input_tokens > 0` and (b) `cost_cents = 0, cost_status = 'unpriced', input_tokens > 0`, the two rows are distinguishable in the `by-agent-model` response without inspecting any other field.
- [ ] `server/src/__tests__/costs-service.test.ts` covers the case above for `byAgentModel` and for `summary`'s `unpricedEventCount`.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter server test costs-service` passes.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @paperclipai/shared build` passes with the new fields on the `CostByAgentModel` / `CostSummary` types.
- [ ] Backward compatible: existing response fields are unchanged; no new field is required by existing clients.

## Not in scope

- Changing `resolveLedgerCostStatus` semantics. It is correct as written.
- Pricing any `unpriced` model. Surfacing the state is the ask; deciding a price is a per-model decision.
- `runCountsByBillingType` on the read endpoints — that is #11422, and this issue should be additive to it rather than overlapping it.

## Related

- #5598 — asks for a "NULL-usage guardrail" on paid models. That is this same `costStatus` primitive, asked for from the alerting side. Worth cross-linking; the two should not be implemented twice.
- #11566 — quotes `heartbeat_runs.usage_json` carrying `costStatus: "reported"` while `cost_cents` reads `0`, i.e. the same lost distinction from the opposite direction.
- #11422 — sibling gap on the `billingType` axis (run counts); same shape, different column.

## Why this was not fixed in place by the reporter

The reporter runs a self-hosted `2026.916.1` from the `npx` cache. Patching the cache is reverted by any restart and would be an unowned change to a running production server, so this is reported upstream rather than patched.
